solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Bring out ecstasy sanctioned by law (6)

annotation.surface: A drug that has somehow been made legal is brought out.
annotation.walkthrough: E is standard shorthand for the drug ecstasy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to draw a reaction or a fact out of someone.

entries.clue: Make happy when abolishing penny rent (5)

indicators.note: abolishing the penny does away with its P

blocks.note: to please is to make happy
p is the abbreviation for a penny; it is removed

annotation.surface: A tenant is delighted that the penny rent has been scrapped.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads "penny rent" as a tiny rent; in fact the penny is the P removed, and rent stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: paying to use a property for a fixed term is renting it.

entries.clue: Attlee maybe being merciful (7)

blocks.note: the first name of Attlee, Labour prime minister 1945-51
an adjective for lenient, showing mercy

annotation.surface: A remark that a former prime minister is showing mercy.
annotation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was Britain's Labour prime minister from 1945 to 1951; "maybe" flags that he is just one example of a Clement.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: Attlee's first name, and an adjective for mild or lenient, as a judge or the weather can be.

entries.clue: Endlessly carry small child (3)

indicators.note: without its end: the last letter goes

blocks.note: to tote is to carry; drop its last letter

annotation.surface: A parent forever lugging a toddler about.
annotation.walkthrough: "Endlessly" looks like an adverb for carrying; it trims the final E.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an affectionate word for a toddler or very young child.

entries.clue: Boost following quiet approval (6)

indicators.note: the boost comes after the quiet letter

annotation.surface: A morale boost that comes after some low-key approval.
annotation.walkthrough: P for quiet comes from musical notation (piano, softly).
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: approval or admiration spoken out loud about someone.

entries.clue: Part of volume about crime in church establishment (9)

indicators.note: the page goes around the crime

blocks.note: a page is part of a book

annotation.surface: A chapter of a history recounting a crime committed in a church.
annotation.walkthrough: Volume hints at loudness, but here it is a book, and the crime sits inside one of its leaves.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the house a church provides for its parish priest.

entries.clue: Director of public school in East End (5)

indicators.note: Cockney speech of London's East End drops the initial H

blocks.note: Harrow is a famous English public (private) school; lose the H

annotation.surface: The head of a posh school located in a working-class part of London.
annotation.walkthrough: The Director is not a headteacher but something that directs you. Cockneys from London's East End traditionally drop their Hs.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a sign pointing the way directs you, so it can be called a director.

entries.clue: Aunt Sal cooked dried fruit (7)

indicators.note: cooked letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A relative bakes something with dried fruit in it.
annotation.walkthrough: Aunt Sal looks like a person in the kitchen; her letters rearrange into the fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a small seedless raisin, one kind of dried fruit used in cakes and buns.

entries.clue: Initially met a more methodical killer? (3-5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of the next word

annotation.surface: A question about whether an orderly person one first met is a murderer.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the answer is only one kind of killer, a tiger or shark, say.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a tiger or shark that attacks people is one kind of killer, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Government regret keeping Labour’s leader (4)

indicators.note: the regret holds the letter inside it
the leader of Labour is its first letter

annotation.surface: Voters come to regret a government with a Labour leader.
annotation.walkthrough: Labour is a British political party, which makes the political surface convincing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: governing a country, as in home rule or the rule of a monarch.

entries.clue: Give up, taken in by police detail (4)

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the next words

annotation.surface: Someone surrenders after being arrested by a police squad.
annotation.walkthrough: A police detail is a squad assigned a task, but here the words just carry the letters across their join.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to surrender territory or a point in argument.

entries.clue: Shoes perhaps are of two shapes (8)

indicators.note: the letters are given a new shape

annotation.surface: An observation that shoes come in two forms, left and right.
annotation.walkthrough: "shapes" reads as a noun in the surface, but it works as a verb telling you to reshape the letters before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: shoes are one kind of thing worn on the feet, alongside boots and sandals.

entries.clue: Scores holding African country ceremony (9)

indicators.note: the number holds the country inside it

annotation.surface: Crowds at an African state occasion.
annotation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so the plural "Scores" is the setter's loose shorthand for two of them; the surface reads it as crowds.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a ceremony is an occasion bound by rules of form and procedure.

entries.clue: One offering insight keeping non-drinking dog (6)

indicators.note: the prophet keeps TT inside

annotation.surface: A prophet who keeps a teetotal dog.
annotation.walkthrough: TT (teetotal) is a standard abbreviation for someone who does not drink alcohol.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the English, Irish and Gordon breeds are gun dogs trained to point at game.

entries.clue: Possibly hate having made changes to omit one (7)

indicators.note: the letters are changed around

annotation.surface: Someone who hates having to leave something out after making edits.
annotation.walkthrough: "Possibly" signals that hate is only one example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: hate is one strong feeling among many, as are love and fear.

entries.clue: Where planes fly over area of golf course — but not loud (6)

indicators.note: 'but not loud' means the course area without its loud letter, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: the fairway is the mown stretch between tee and green
f (forte) means loud in music; it is removed

annotation.surface: Planes flying quietly over a golf course.
annotation.walkthrough: F for loud comes from musical notation (forte).
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a route through the sky that aircraft are directed to follow.

entries.clue: Book place to see game (7)

blocks.note: the verb, as in booking a table in advance
a park where game (wild animals) is protected and viewed

annotation.surface: Buying a ticket for a match at a stadium.
annotation.walkthrough: "Game" suggests a sporting match, but it means wild animals, as on a safari.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: the verb for booking a seat or table, and a protected area where wild animals can be viewed.

entries.clue: Way speed is limited (8)

blocks.note: a mode is a way of doing something

annotation.surface: A statement that the pace on a road is capped.
annotation.walkthrough: "Way" looks like a road, but it is a manner of doing something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: kept within reasonable limits, neither large nor extreme.

entries.clue: Bush senior (5)

blocks.note: a shrub with white flowers and dark berries
older, as in the older of two siblings

annotation.surface: George H. W. Bush, the father of the later President Bush.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at the US presidents; in fact Bush is a shrub and senior means older.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: a shrub with white flowers and dark berries, and an adjective for the older of two people.

entries.clue: Dismiss rather shapeless dress (4)

blocks.note: informal verb for firing someone from a job
a loose dress without a waist

annotation.surface: Rejecting a baggy frock.
annotation.walkthrough: The dress sense is a loose style that hangs straight from the shoulders, named for its resemblance to a bag.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: an informal verb for firing an employee, and a loose dress that hangs straight without a waist.

entries.clue: Preserve a lake waterway (5)

blocks.note: to can food is to preserve it
L is the map abbreviation for lake

annotation.surface: A call to protect a lake and its waterway.
annotation.walkthrough: "Preserve" suggests conservation, but here it means putting food in a tin.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: an artificial channel dug for boats is one kind of waterway.

entries.clue: Look after home in outskirts of Milford (4)

indicators.note: the home goes inside the outer letters
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of Milford

annotation.surface: Taking care of a house on the edge of a town called Milford.
annotation.walkthrough: IN for home is a crossword convention: staying in means staying at home.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to take care of children or a shop for a while, as a babysitter does.

entries.clue: Train gone? Nearly frantic, not knowing (8)

indicators.note: drop the last letter of gone
frantic letters are in a wild jumble

blocks.note: used as is in the mix

annotation.surface: A passenger panicking on the platform, unsure whether the train has left.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark and comma break the clue into a scene; ignore them and the train and nearly-gone letters go into the mix together.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lacking knowledge, unaware of something.

entries.clue: Pinch a drink (3)

blocks.note: to squeeze sharply between finger and thumb
a small measure of spirits such as whisky

annotation.surface: Stealing a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pinch" reads as steal in the surface; here it means squeeze.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: a verb for a sharp squeeze, and a noun for a small measure of spirits.

entries.clue: Dynamism new in excerpt from Peer Gynt (6)

indicators.note: the N goes inside the excerpt
the letters are lifted out of the next words

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new

annotation.surface: Fresh vitality in a passage from Ibsen's play Peer Gynt.
annotation.walkthrough: Peer Gynt is Ibsen's play; the excerpt straddles the break between its two words, and N slips in after its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: vigour and drive, the quality that gets things done.

entries.clue: Unusual all pea dish (6)

indicators.note: the letters are put in an unusual order

annotation.surface: An odd meal made entirely of peas.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a dish of nothing but peas; the letters rebuild a Spanish classic.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a Spanish rice dish from Valencia, cooked with saffron, seafood or meat.
